out.text: Yes, the red slope is in the right place: horizontal, against the left edge of the plate, with empty studs above and below it. I've confirmed step 1.

Not yet. The purple brick is lying horizontally, four studs long and two tall, when it should stand vertically: two studs wide and four tall. It also sits lower than the red slope rather than rising one stud above its top. Turn it upright so its bottom lines up with the slope's bottom and its top sticks one stud above the slope.
The purple 2x4 is vertical and touches the right side of the red slope. Its top sits one stud above the slope's top, and its bottom is level with the slope's bottom. This step is right.

Not yet. The plate shows the red slope and purple brick, but no lime brick. Place the lime one-by-two vertically against the right side of the purple brick's top, so it sticks out one stud above the purple.

Not quite. The lime piece sits flush with the top of the purple brick instead of sticking out one stud above it. It also looks about as tall as the purple brick, so it may be a longer piece. Move it so it's two studs tall, touching the purple brick's right side, with its top one stud above the purple top. If it's already in that spot, a closer photo would help me confirm.
The lime one-by-two is standing vertically against the right side of the purple brick at its top, and its top sits one stud above the purple brick. That matches step 3.

The brick right of the purple one is beige or tan, not pure white, so step 4 isn't right yet. Swap it for the white one-by-six (the tan one is for step 11). Its left end should touch the purple brick, directly below the lime exhaust.
Yes, the white one-by-six now lies horizontally right of the purple brick, touching it, with its left end at the purple brick and directly below the lime exhaust.

Not yet: I don't see a vertical white one-by-four on the plate yet. The right end of the body is still bare, and the white piece is in your hand. Place it vertically against the right ends of the two white bricks and the lime brick, one stud above the top white brick.

Not yet. The right wheel sits too far right, under the end of the white brick, and there are about seven or eight empty studs between it and the left wheel instead of three. Slide it left so it sits under the blue and lime bricks, with three empty columns to the left wheel and bare plate under the white end.

Not yet. The right wheel has four empty stud columns between it and the left wheel, not three. Slide it one stud left so it touches the blue and lime bricks with three empty columns between the wheels. Bare plate should still show below the white brick at the right end.
Yes, that's the last brick. The yellow one-by-four sits in the ground row, touching the white ground brick, and its right end reaches the plate's right edge. I'm confirming step 13.
The brick in your right hand is a purple one, held at its near end. It's not on the plate yet, so step 2 isn't built.
There are three red pieces on the plate: the red slope on the left edge and the two red wheel discs below it.

Both are red discs of the same design, and they should both be four studs across. The left one looks a bit larger only because it sits nearer the camera. The tan ground brick isn't on the plate yet, so step 11 is still open.
The red slope is against the left edge of the plate, lying horizontally with four studs across and three up and down. It is red, with empty plate above and below it. Step 1 is right.

No, the purple brick is lying horizontally. It should stand vertically, taller than it is wide, with its bottom level with the red slope's bottom and its top one stud above the slope's top. Turn it upright so it runs up and down.
The purple 2x4 is vertical, touches the right side of the red slope, and its bottom lines up with the slope's bottom. Its top sits one stud above the slope's top, so step 2 is right.

Not yet: there's no lime brick on the plate yet. The red slope and purple brick are in place, but nothing sits to the right of the purple brick's top. Take the small lime one-by-two, stand it vertically against the purple brick's right side at the top, with its top one stud above the purple brick.
Not yet. The lime brick is standing right of the purple brick, but its top is level with the purple's top. It should sit one stud higher, so its top sticks up one stud above the purple brick.
The lime 1x2 is vertical, touching the right side of the purple brick at its top, and its top sits one stud above the purple brick's top. That matches step 3.

The brick right of the purple one looks beige or tan, not pure white. The white bricks on the table look clearly brighter. Please swap it for the white one-by-six and show it closer if it's already white.
Yes, the white one-by-six is now right: it lies horizontally against the right side of the purple brick, six studs long, directly below the lime exhaust. I'm confirming step 4.

Not yet. The plate shows no vertical white one-by-four at the right end of the body. The lime brick sits at the right end of the blue row, and the white bricks end beside it with nothing standing against them. The white piece in your right hand isn't on the plate. Place the white one-by-four vertically against those right ends, one stud above the top white brick, then I can check it.

Not yet. The right wheel sits about seven studs from the left wheel, but it should have three empty columns between them. Slide it left so its top still touches the blue and lime bricks, and keep the plate bare below the white brick at the right end.

Not confirmed yet. The right wheel sits below the blue and lime bricks, but the gap between it and the left wheel looks closer to four empty columns than three. The photo is at an angle, so I can't be certain. Please move the right wheel one stud left and show the plate from directly above, so I can count the gap.
Yes, the yellow one-by-four is the last piece, sitting in the ground row right of the white brick and reaching the right edge of the plate. I'm confirming step 13.
The brick in your right hand is purple, a stud-topped brick, most likely the purple 2x4 for this step. It isn't on the plate yet, so the step isn't checked.
There are three red pieces on the plate: the red slope on the left edge and the two red wheels below it.

The two wheels appear to be the same red disc. The left one looks a little larger only because it sits nearer the camera. Step 11 isn't built yet, since the tan brick isn't on the plate in this photo.
Yes, the red slope is against the left edge of the plate, lying horizontally with empty plate above and below it. I'm confirming step 1.

Not yet. The purple brick is lying horizontally and sits slightly low. It needs to stand vertically, two studs wide and four tall, touching the slope's right side, with its bottom level with the slope's bottom so its top sticks out one stud above the slope.
The purple 2x4 sits vertically directly right of the red slope and touches it. Its bottom is level with the slope's bottom, and its top is about one stud above the slope's top.

No, not yet. The plate shows only the red slope and the purple brick, with no lime green brick beside the purple brick's top. The lime one-by-two still needs to go vertically on the right side of the purple brick, sticking one stud above it.

Not right yet: the lime piece on the right of the purple brick runs level with the purple's full height and doesn't stick out above it. It should be a vertical one-by-two whose top is one stud above the purple brick's top.
The lime one-by-two is vertical, touching the right side of the purple brick at its top, and sticks out one stud above it. That matches step 3.

Not yet: the brick on the plate right of the purple brick looks beige or tan, not pure white. It sits in the right row, touching the purple brick below the lime exhaust. Swap it for the white one-by-six. If it is white and I'm misreading the colour, bring it closer to the camera so I can check.
Yes, the white one-by-six now lies horizontally to the right of the purple brick, its left end touching it, directly below the lime exhaust.

Not yet. The plate has no vertical white brick at the right end of the white bricks. The white piece in your right hand is too small to be the one-by-four. Place the white one-by-four vertically against the right ends of the white bricks and the lime brick, one stud above the top white brick.

Not yet. The right wheel sits too far right, mostly under the white brick's right end, when it should be under the blue and lime bricks. There are about six or seven empty columns between the two wheels, not three. Slide it about four studs left so its top touches the blue and lime bricks, and leave the plate bare below the white end brick.

The right wheel is below the body and touches the blue and lime bricks, but the gap to the left wheel looks like about four empty studs, not three. Shift it one stud toward the left wheel, keeping it touching the blue and lime bricks. The photo is at an angle, so if you count three columns on the plate, show me a closer, straight-on photo.
Yes, the yellow one-by-four is in the ground row, touching the white ground brick and running flush to the right edge of the plate. That completes the truck, and this was the last step.
You're holding a purple LEGO brick between your fingers, the one on the right side of the photo. It looks like the purple piece for step 2, but I can't clearly count its studs from here.
There are three red pieces on the plate: the red slope on the left edge and the two red wheel discs below it.

They look like the same red disc, both about four studs across. The left one appears a little bigger only because it sits closer to the camera. The current step is still the tan brick, which hasn't been placed yet.
